description.narrative:
The overall objective of this contribution is to strengthening the health system in Somalia by supporting the building and strengthening of essential public health functions.
The specific objective of the intervention is to:
1) Support the establishment of an independent National Institute for Health (NIH) in Somalia, and;
2) Strengthening the Health Management Information System (HMIS) in pilot locations across Somalia, as well as working towards the development of an integrated disease surveillance and response system in Somalia.

Denna insats skall ge finansiellt stöd till WHO Somalia och har som huvudsyfte att med WHO:s tekniska expertis stödja två andra svenska insatser som implementeras i Somalia, nämligen utvecklandet av en Somalisk Folkhälsomyndighet som sker i ett samarbete med den svenska folkhälsomyndigheten och att digitalisera Somalias hälsohanteringsinformationssystem som sker genom ett samarbete med Stockholms Universitet/SPIDER. Insatsen bygger dels på de arbetsplaner som WHO har överenskommit med folkhälsomyndigheten och med Stockholms universitet/SPIDER och dels på de arbetsbeskrivningar som tagits fram för de två experter som kommer stödja implementeringen.

This contribution will provide financial support to WHO Somalia to allow WHO to dedicate technical expertise two other Swedish initiatives implemented in Somalia and has as its main purpose to support two other Swedish initiatives implemented in Somalia, namely the development of a Somali Public Health Agency in collaboration with the Swedish Public Health Agency and to digitilize Somalia's health management information system which takes place through a collaboration with Stockholm University / SPIDER. The contribution is based on both the work plans that the WHO has agreed with the public health authority and with Stockholm University / SPIDER and also on the job descriptions prepared for the two experts WHO will provide to support the implementation.

The collaboration Sweden's support to WHO consisted of a senior Health Systems Advisor seconded from Public Health Agency of Sweden (PHAS), based in Nairobi, for one year; as well as a Health Systems Officer and a Surveillance Officer (national staff), in Somalia, for four years.
The overall objective was to strengthen synergies between the ongoing PHAS project and SPIDER project and ongoing WHO activities on common fields of action. An Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between PHAS and WHO was established early on outlining joint and complementary support to the development of the National Institute of Health and its public health functions. An MoU between SPIDER and WHO was also agreed, consisting of complementary support to development in the health information system.
As noted by the WHO, the support provided by Sweden to WHO Somalia was catalytic, as it impacted the use and effectiveness of bigger resources. WHO also highlighted that considering the country context in the past years, Sweden's support was and remained relevant despite disruption, thanks to its flexibility.
Examples of results:
- Support in operationalizing the National Institute of Health (NIH) - Developed NIH Operational Plan (2021 -2023) and supported in implementation, from physical working space, website and visibility, to actual public health functions. - Established the Field Epidemiology Training Program. Sweden funded the very first cohort in 2021. Over 400 staff trained, also with other support. - Established the Integrated Disease Surveillance and Response System - Integration of the DHIS2 platform for real-time data collection and reporting. - Capacity to detect and respond to major outbreaks within 24 hours of reporting. - Strengthened Health Management Information Systems - HIS strategic plan developed and in use - Strengthened research capacity - Continuous support to HIS technical working group
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
